record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Extend renormalization-group methods to hyperbolic equations.

evidence.quote: The major open problems listed in [BK2] are... extension of renormalization group methods to hyperbolic equations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Renormalization-group (RG) techniques have been highly successful in analyzing the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions to nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations of the form
$$\partial_t u = \mathcal{L} u + F(u,\nabla u,\ldots), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d,\ t>0,$$
where $\mathcal{L}$ is a (possibly fractional) elliptic operator and $F$ is a nonlinear term. In this setting, one introduces a scaling transformation $u(x,t)\mapsto L^{\alpha} u(Lx,L^{2}t)$ acting on initial data at time $t=1$, and iterates the resulting map on a suitable Banach space of initial conditions; fixed points of the iteration correspond to self-similar asymptotic profiles, and the spectrum of the linearization classifies relevant, marginal, and irrelevant perturbations. This framework yields rigorous results on stability of fronts, anomalous scaling, and blow-up profiles.

Problem. Develop an analogous rigorous renormalization-group framework for nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations, for instance equations of the form
$$\partial_t^2 u - \Delta u = F(u,\partial u),\qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}_+,$$
or first-order symmetric hyperbolic systems $\partial_t U + \sum_{j} A_j\,\partial_{x_j} U = F(U)$. Specifically: define an appropriate scaling transformation acting on Cauchy data (or on data posed on a characteristic surface), identify function spaces on which the induced RG map is well-defined and contractive in a neighborhood of self-similar profiles, classify the relevant/marginal/irrelevant directions of the linearized RG map, and use this construction to prove results on long-time asymptotics, stability of self-similar solutions, formation of singularities, or universality of scaling near blow-up for nonlinear hyperbolic PDEs, parallel to what is known in the parabolic case.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature documents extensive successful applications of rigorous renormalization-group methods to nonlinear parabolic PDEs (Bricmont–Kupiainen–Lin, Ginzburg–Landau equation, reaction-diffusion, blow-up profiles) and more recently to stochastic PDEs, but no analogous general RG framework for nonlinear hyperbolic equations was located. The problem of extending RG methods to hyperbolic equations remains listed as a major open problem and appears to be still open.

status_evidence.title: Renormalization Group and Asymptotics of Solutions of Nonlinear Parabolic Equations
status_evidence.snippet: General method for studying long time asymptotics of nonlinear parabolic PDEs via RG; applications to Ginzburg-Landau, reaction-diffusion, blow-up.
status_evidence.claim: Existing rigorous RG-for-PDE results are restricted to parabolic-type equations.

status_evidence.title: Renormalization Group and Stochastic PDEs
status_evidence.snippet: RG techniques applied to stochastic (parabolic) PDEs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions go to stochastic parabolic PDEs, not to hyperbolic ones.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to the Renormalization Group (Kupiainen lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes surveying RG methods, focused on parabolic and stochastic settings.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys by leading practitioners do not present an RG framework for hyperbolic PDEs.
